description: prHourlyLimit is 0 (unlimited), overriding Renovate's default of 2. That default
exists to keep busy public repos from flooding a PR list and burning API quota;
here it only hides work. This repo runs weekly, so a batch larger than two gets
trickled out two PRs at a time a week apart, and the remainder sit in the
Dependency Dashboard's Rate-Limited section — no PR, no error, easy to read as
'Renovate found nothing'. That happened on 2026-09-26: the linuxserver versioning
fix detected all five images, but sonarr/radarr/prowlarr were capped out and never
filed. prConcurrentLimit stays at its default of 10 as the real backstop on how
many updates are open at once.
Portainer is bootstrapped with `docker run` (docs/INSTALL.md) rather than as a Stack —
it is what deploys the Stacks — so its pin lives in prose no built-in manager
parses. Without this it would rot silently.
LinuxServer.io images never update under Renovate's default `docker` versioning.
That scheme splits a tag at the first `-` and treats the remainder as a
'compatibility' string (the `-alpine` / `-bookworm` convention), then only offers
tags carrying the identical string. LinuxServer's suffix is its own build counter
— `-ls155` -> `-ls162` — so no candidate ever matches and every linuxserver/*
image sits frozen: no PR, no warning, nothing on the Dependency Dashboard.
Hence explicit regex versioning, which folds that counter into the version.
It goes into `build`, deliberately, NOT the more obvious `revision`: regex
versioning only appends `revision` to the comparable release when `build` also
matched (modules/versioning/regex/index.js). With the counter in `revision`,
any image whose tag has no fourth numeric segment — qbittorrent, jellyfin —
parses to a bare major.minor.patch, so the counter is dropped and every ls-only
rebuild still compares equal. Same silent freeze, one layer deeper.
`[^-]*` absorbs whatever sits between the app version and the counter, which is
a different thing per image and needs no ordering of its own:
sonarr/radarr/prowlarr  4.0.19.2979-ls320      upstream build number
qbittorrent             5.2.3_v2.0.13-ls469    bundled libtorrent
jellyfin                10.11.11ubu2604-ls43   base-distro tag
jellyfin 12.x           12.1ubu2604-ls50       two-segment, no patch
Ordering on the ls counter alone is safe because LinuxServer increments it per
build and never resets it across upstream version changes.
Requiring a leading digit and a literal `-ls` is also what keeps `develop`,
`nightly`, `amd64-*`/`arm64v8-*` and the bare rolling `2.6.5` tags out of the
candidate set.
Built on the NAS from this repo (scripts/build-images.sh), never pushed to a
registry: every lookup fails ('no-result') and shows as a warning on the
Dependency Dashboard. Its tag changes with the code, not with Renovate.
